newsitem.title: USA: Utilities told focus should be on customer growth.
newsitem.headline: Utilities told focus should be on customer growth.

text.p: With earnings projections largely flat, investor-owned electric utilities in the U.S. need to look at ways to increase their customer base, industry experts said at a conference here on Tuesday.
"With competition growing, talk about market share quickly becomes passe," said Thomas Flaherty, a partner at Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group. "Utilities need to think about their customer base."
John Hayes, chairman of Western Resources Inc. said "value will be built in non-traditional ways."
He cited cross-selling to customers within Western's non- utility businesses as a key element of this strategy.
"The commodity won't drive value. It's everything you add on to it," said Flaherty.
He said a good analogy would be the cellular phone industry, where per customer value skyrocked from around $12 to $300 over a short period.
"The commodity is a loss-leader or a giveaway. The growth will be in total service," Flaherty said.
He noted the number of participants in the power and natural gas markets will continue to decline as efficiency- related consolidations take place.
But there may also be bankruptcies in the industry, depending "on whether we get national legislation on retail wheeling or go state by state," Flaherty noted.
